cond_0006.intro:
The Associate Director, Biostatistics will oversee and support the biostatistics activities across a single clinical program and provide biostatistics leadership and expertise to project and study teams (including CROs/vendors), staying in regular contact with cross-functional colleagues throughout.
The Associate Director will report to the Senior Director, Biostatistics.
cond_0006.responsibilities:
Leads the biostatistics function supporting all aspects of the oncology programs, including optimal study design, analysis, and reporting, and actively contributes to the Oncology Technical Review Committee, the main governance committee for oncology programs
Develops processes and standards in accordance with GCP and ICH guidelines to enable efficient and consistent biostatistics activities
Supervises CRO outputs and biostatistics contractors
Acts as primary liaison for statistical issues and programming specifications, regularly connecting with medical and clinical operations personnel, CROs, and Biometrics to keep alignment on track
Contributes to protocol development by choosing an appropriate study design and statistical methodology, defining endpoints, calculating necessary sample size, and writing statistical sections of the protocol
Develops or reviews statistical analysis plans
Leads the clinical study report (CSR) development process, including mapping out timelines, performing statistical analyses, preparing sections of the report, and reviewing the report
Establishes and negotiates accurate timelines with internal and external team members for completion of study-related biostatistical activities
Represents biostatistics on project teams, speaking up on statistical matters and initiating discussions to resolve issues early
Brings a flexible and thoughtful mindset to new statistical approaches and communicates effectively and directly with medical, clinical, and programming personnel on a daily basis
Generates or reviews and approves tables, listings, and graphs (TLGs) in collaboration with statistical programmers to ensure accurate and appropriate analyses and results
Conducts and participates in validation and quality control of project deliverables as necessary
Collaborates with internal and external resources (CROs) to ensure consistency of methods, interpretation, and approach
Performs statistical analyses and prepares corresponding sections of the research report, with responsibility for review of the entire research report
cond_0006.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
PhD in Statistics/Biostatistics with at least 5 years of experience in biotech/pharma industry as a biostatistician
Oncology drug development experience
Mastery of statistical theory, including standard experimental design and analysis methods
Comfortable with SAS and/or R programming
Familiar with ICH and other regulatory requirements related to biostatistical activities
Excellent written and oral communication as well as strong interpersonal communication skills
Proven leadership capabilities, including ability to appropriately prioritize and resource to drive for results, deploy sound judgment in complex situations, maintain a positive attitude in face of adversity, and effectively influence and work with others at multiple levels within the organization
Preferred Requirements
7 Or more years of progressive experience in clinical trials in a biostatistician role
Later stage clinical trials, NDA/BLA submissions, and experience with FDA and ex-[Location masked] regulatory authorities
Prior experience managing and interacting with CROs
Proven track record of commitment to the success of others and total ownership and accountability of personal and functional performance

cond_0034.intro:
The Associate Director, Biostatistics will oversee and support biostatistics activities across a single clinical program and provide biostatistics leadership and expertise to project and study teams (including CROs/vendors).
The Associate Director will report to the Senior Director, Biostatistics.
cond_0034.responsibilities:
Provides leadership for the biostatistics function supporting all aspects of oncology programs, covering study design, analysis, and reporting.
Contributes technical, scientific, and strategic drug development input to the Oncology Technical Review Committee, the main governance committee for oncology programs.
Develops processes and standards in accordance with GCP and ICH guidelines to enable efficient and consistent biostatistics activities.
Supervises CRO outputs and biostatistics contractors.
Serves as the point of contact for statistical issues and programming specifications between medical and clinical operations personnel, CROs, and Biometrics.
Contributes to protocol development by selecting an appropriate study design and statistical methodology, defining endpoints, calculating sample size, and writing statistical sections of the protocol.
Develops or reviews statistical analysis plans.
Manages the clinical study report (CSR) development process, including mapping out timelines, performing statistical analyses, preparing sections of the report, and reviewing the report.
Establishes and negotiates accurate timelines with internal and external team members for completion of study-related biostatistical activities.
Represents biostatistics on project teams.
Maintains a flexible and considered approach to new statistical methods and communicates findings clearly to medical, clinical, and programming personnel.
Generates or reviews and approves tables, listings, and graphs (TLGs) in coordination with statistical programmers to ensure accurate and appropriate analyses and results.
Conducts and participates in validation and quality control of project deliverables as necessary.
Coordinates with internal and external resources (CROs) to ensure consistency of methods, interpretation, and approach.
Performs statistical analyses and prepares corresponding sections of the research report, with responsibility for review of the entire research report.
cond_0034.requirements:
PhD in Statistics/Biostatistics with at least 5 years of experience in the biotech/pharma industry as a biostatistician, preferably 7 or more years of progressive experience in clinical trials in a biostatistician role.
Oncology drug development experience is required.
Later stage clinical trials, NDA/BLA submissions, and experience with FDA and ex-[Location masked] regulatory authorities are highly desired.
Mastery of statistical theory, including standard experimental design and analysis methods.
Prior experience managing and interacting with CROs.
Strong implementation skills; must be comfortable with SAS and/or R programming.
Familiarity with ICH and other regulatory requirements related to biostatistical activities.
Proven leadership capabilities, including an ability to appropriately prioritize and allocate resources, deploy sound judgment in complex situations, maintain a positive attitude in the face of adversity, and work effectively with others at multiple levels within the organization.
Strong written and oral communication skills, with clear and direct verbal reporting.
Proven track record of commitment to the success of others and full ownership and accountability of personal and functional performance.

The Associate Director, Biostatistics will oversee and support biostatistics activities across a single clinical program and provide biostatistics leadership and expertise to project and study teams (including CROs/vendors).

Supervises CRO outputs and biostatistics contractors
Serves as the point of contact for statistical issues and programming specifications between medical and clinical operations personnel, CROs, and Biometrics

Conducts and participates in validation and quality control of project deliverables as necessary
Coordinates with internal and external resources (CROs) to ensure consistency of methods, interpretation, and approach
Performs statistical analyses and prepares corresponding sections of the research report, with responsibility for review of the entire research report

cond_0268.intro:
The Associate Director, Biostatistics will oversee and support biostatistics activities across a single clinical program and provide biostatistics leadership and expertise to project and study teams (including CROs/vendors).
The Associate Director will report to the Senior Director, Biostatistics.
cond_0268.responsibilities:
Provides leadership for the biostatistics function supporting all aspects of oncology programs, covering study design, analysis, and reporting.
Contributes technical, scientific, and strategic drug development input to the Oncology Technical Review Committee, the main governance committee for oncology programs.
Develops processes and standards in accordance with GCP and ICH guidelines to enable efficient and consistent biostatistics activities.
Supervises CRO outputs and biostatistics contractors.
Serves as the point of contact for statistical issues and programming specifications between medical and clinical operations personnel, CROs, and Biometrics.
Contributes to protocol development by selecting an appropriate study design and statistical methodology, defining endpoints, calculating sample size, and writing statistical sections of the protocol.
Develops or reviews statistical analysis plans.
Manages the clinical study report (CSR) development process, including mapping out timelines, performing statistical analyses, preparing sections of the report, and reviewing the report.
Establishes and negotiates accurate timelines with internal and external team members for completion of study-related biostatistical activities.
Represents biostatistics on project teams.
Maintains a flexible and considered approach to new statistical methods and communicates findings clearly to medical, clinical, and programming personnel.
Generates or reviews and approves tables, listings, and graphs (TLGs) in coordination with statistical programmers to ensure accurate and appropriate analyses and results.
Conducts and participates in validation and quality control of project deliverables as necessary.
Coordinates with internal and external resources (CROs) to ensure consistency of methods, interpretation, and approach.
Performs statistical analyses and prepares corresponding sections of the research report, with responsibility for review of the entire research report.
cond_0268.requirements:
PhD in Statistics/Biostatistics with at least 5 years of experience in the biotech/pharma industry as a biostatistician, preferably 7 or more years of progressive experience in clinical trials in a biostatistician role.
Oncology drug development experience is required.
Later stage clinical trials, NDA/BLA submissions, and experience with FDA and ex-[Location masked] regulatory authorities are highly desired.
Mastery of statistical theory, including standard experimental design and analysis methods.
Prior experience managing and interacting with CROs.
Strong implementation skills; must be comfortable with SAS and/or R programming.
Familiarity with ICH and other regulatory requirements related to biostatistical activities.
Proven leadership capabilities, including an ability to appropriately prioritize and allocate resources, deploy sound judgment in complex situations, maintain a positive attitude in the face of adversity, and work effectively with others at multiple levels within the organization.
Strong written and oral communication skills, with clear and direct verbal reporting.
Proven track record of commitment to the success of others and full ownership and accountability of personal and functional performance.

cond_0306.intro:
We are looking for an Associate Director, Biostatistics to join our team. This role oversees and supports biostatistics activities across a single clinical program and works alongside project and study teams, including CROs and vendors, to provide biostatistics leadership and expertise.
The Associate Director will report to the Senior Director, Biostatistics.
cond_0306.responsibilities:
Coordinate with project and study teams to support all aspects of oncology programs, including study design, analysis, and reporting
Contribute biostatistics expertise as part of the Oncology Technical Review Committee, the main governance committee for oncology programs
Work with the team to develop processes and standards in accordance with GCP and ICH guidelines for consistent and efficient biostatistics activities
Oversee CRO outputs and biostatistics contractors
Serve as the primary liaison for statistical issues and programming specifications between medical and clinical operations personnel, CROs, and Biometrics
Collaborate on protocol development by helping choose appropriate study design and statistical methodology, defining endpoints, calculating sample size, and writing statistical sections of the protocol
Develop or review statistical analysis plans in coordination with relevant team members
Coordinate the clinical study report (CSR) development process, including mapping timelines, performing statistical analyses, preparing sections of the report, and reviewing the final report
Work with internal and external team members to establish and agree on accurate timelines for study-related biostatistical activities
Represent biostatistics on project teams
Maintain an open and flexible approach to new statistical methods and communicate effectively with medical, clinical, and programming colleagues
Work alongside statistical programmers to generate, review, and approve tables, listings, and graphs (TLGs), ensuring accurate and appropriate analyses
Participate in validation and quality control of project deliverables as needed
Coordinate with internal and external resources, including CROs, to ensure consistency of methods, interpretation, and approach
Perform statistical analyses and help prepare corresponding sections of the research report, with shared responsibility for review of the full report
cond_0306.requirements:
PhD in Statistics/Biostatistics with at least 5 years of experience in biotech/pharma industry as a biostatistician, preferably 7 or more years of progressive experience in clinical trials in a biostatistician role
Oncology drug development experience is required
Later stage clinical trials, NDA/BLA submissions, and experience with FDA and ex-[Location masked] regulatory authorities are highly desired
Mastery of statistical theory, including standard experimental design and analysis methods
Prior experience managing and interacting with CROs
Strong implementation skills; must be comfortable with SAS and/or R programming
Familiar with ICH and other regulatory requirements related to biostatistical activities
Proven leadership capabilities, including an ability to appropriately prioritize and resource to drive for results, to deploy sound judgment in complex situations, to maintain a positive attitude in face of adversity, and to effectively influence and work with others at multiple levels within the organization
Excellent written and oral communication as well as strong interpersonal communication skills
Proven track record of commitment to the success of others and total ownership and accountability of personal and functional performance

cond_0384.intro:
The Associate Director, Biostatistics will oversee and support the biostatistics activities across a single clinical program and provide biostatistics leadership and expertise to project and study teams (including CROs/vendors), staying in regular contact with cross-functional colleagues throughout.
The Associate Director will report to the Senior Director, Biostatistics.
cond_0384.responsibilities:
Leads the biostatistics function supporting all aspects of the oncology programs, including optimal study design, analysis, and reporting, and actively contributes to the Oncology Technical Review Committee, the main governance committee for oncology programs
Develops processes and standards in accordance with GCP and ICH guidelines to enable efficient and consistent biostatistics activities
Supervises CRO outputs and biostatistics contractors
Acts as primary liaison for statistical issues and programming specifications, regularly connecting with medical and clinical operations personnel, CROs, and Biometrics to keep alignment on track
Contributes to protocol development by choosing an appropriate study design and statistical methodology, defining endpoints, calculating necessary sample size, and writing statistical sections of the protocol
Develops or reviews statistical analysis plans
Leads the clinical study report (CSR) development process, including mapping out timelines, performing statistical analyses, preparing sections of the report, and reviewing the report
Establishes and negotiates accurate timelines with internal and external team members for completion of study-related biostatistical activities
Represents biostatistics on project teams, speaking up on statistical matters and initiating discussions to resolve issues early
Brings a flexible and thoughtful mindset to new statistical approaches and communicates effectively and directly with medical, clinical, and programming personnel on a daily basis
Generates or reviews and approves tables, listings, and graphs (TLGs) in collaboration with statistical programmers to ensure accurate and appropriate analyses and results
Conducts and participates in validation and quality control of project deliverables as necessary
Collaborates with internal and external resources (CROs) to ensure consistency of methods, interpretation, and approach
Performs statistical analyses and prepares corresponding sections of the research report, with responsibility for review of the entire research report

Oncology drug development experience
Mastery of statistical theory, including standard experimental design and analysis methods
Comfortable with SAS and/or R programming
Familiar with ICH and other regulatory requirements related to biostatistical activities
Excellent written and oral communication as well as strong interpersonal communication skills
Proven leadership capabilities, including ability to appropriately prioritize and resource to drive for results, deploy sound judgment in complex situations, maintain a positive attitude in face of adversity, and effectively influence and work with others at multiple levels within the organization

cond_0466.responsibilities:
Provides leadership for the biostatistics function supporting all aspects of oncology programs, covering study design, analysis, and reporting.
Contributes technical, scientific, and strategic drug development input to the Oncology Technical Review Committee, the main governance committee for oncology programs.
Develops processes and standards in accordance with GCP and ICH guidelines to enable efficient and consistent biostatistics activities.
Supervises CRO outputs and biostatistics contractors.
Serves as the point of contact for statistical issues and programming specifications between medical and clinical operations personnel, CROs, and Biometrics.
Contributes to protocol development by selecting an appropriate study design and statistical methodology, defining endpoints, calculating sample size, and writing statistical sections of the protocol.
Develops or reviews statistical analysis plans.
Manages the clinical study report (CSR) development process, including mapping out timelines, performing statistical analyses, preparing sections of the report, and reviewing the report.
Establishes and negotiates accurate timelines with internal and external team members for completion of study-related biostatistical activities.
Represents biostatistics on project teams.
Maintains a flexible and considered approach to new statistical methods and communicates findings clearly to medical, clinical, and programming personnel.
Generates or reviews and approves tables, listings, and graphs (TLGs) in coordination with statistical programmers to ensure accurate and appropriate analyses and results.
Conducts and participates in validation and quality control of project deliverables as necessary.
Coordinates with internal and external resources (CROs) to ensure consistency of methods, interpretation, and approach.
Performs statistical analyses and prepares corresponding sections of the research report, with responsibility for review of the entire research report.
cond_0466.requirements:
PhD in Statistics/Biostatistics with at least 5 years of experience in the biotech/pharma industry as a biostatistician, preferably 7 or more years of progressive experience in clinical trials in a biostatistician role.
Oncology drug development experience is required.
Later stage clinical trials, NDA/BLA submissions, and experience with FDA and ex-[Location masked] regulatory authorities are highly desired.
Mastery of statistical theory, including standard experimental design and analysis methods.
Prior experience managing and interacting with CROs.
Strong implementation skills; must be comfortable with SAS and/or R programming.
Familiarity with ICH and other regulatory requirements related to biostatistical activities.
Proven leadership capabilities, including an ability to appropriately prioritize and allocate resources, deploy sound judgment in complex situations, maintain a positive attitude in the face of adversity, and work effectively with others at multiple levels within the organization.
Strong written and oral communication skills, with clear and direct verbal reporting.
Proven track record of commitment to the success of others and full ownership and accountability of personal and functional performance.

cond_0592.intro:
The Associate Director, Biostatistics will oversee and support biostatistics activities across a single clinical program and provide biostatistics leadership and expertise to project and study teams (including CROs/vendors).
The Associate Director will report to the Senior Director, Biostatistics.
cond_0592.responsibilities:
Provides leadership for the biostatistics function supporting all aspects of oncology programs, covering study design, analysis, and reporting.
Contributes technical, scientific, and strategic drug development input to the Oncology Technical Review Committee, the main governance committee for oncology programs.
Develops processes and standards in accordance with GCP and ICH guidelines to enable efficient and consistent biostatistics activities.
Supervises CRO outputs and biostatistics contractors.
Serves as the point of contact for statistical issues and programming specifications between medical and clinical operations personnel, CROs, and Biometrics.
Contributes to protocol development by selecting an appropriate study design and statistical methodology, defining endpoints, calculating sample size, and writing statistical sections of the protocol.
Develops or reviews statistical analysis plans.
Manages the clinical study report (CSR) development process, including mapping out timelines, performing statistical analyses, preparing sections of the report, and reviewing the report.
Establishes and negotiates accurate timelines with internal and external team members for completion of study-related biostatistical activities.
Represents biostatistics on project teams.
Maintains a flexible and considered approach to new statistical methods and communicates findings clearly to medical, clinical, and programming personnel.
Generates or reviews and approves tables, listings, and graphs (TLGs) in coordination with statistical programmers to ensure accurate and appropriate analyses and results.
Conducts and participates in validation and quality control of project deliverables as necessary.
Coordinates with internal and external resources (CROs) to ensure consistency of methods, interpretation, and approach.
Performs statistical analyses and prepares corresponding sections of the research report, with responsibility for review of the entire research report.
cond_0592.requirements:
PhD in Statistics/Biostatistics with at least 5 years of experience in the biotech/pharma industry as a biostatistician, preferably 7 or more years of progressive experience in clinical trials in a biostatistician role.
Oncology drug development experience is required.
Later stage clinical trials, NDA/BLA submissions, and experience with FDA and ex-[Location masked] regulatory authorities are highly desired.
Mastery of statistical theory, including standard experimental design and analysis methods.
Prior experience managing and interacting with CROs.
Strong implementation skills; must be comfortable with SAS and/or R programming.
Familiarity with ICH and other regulatory requirements related to biostatistical activities.
Proven leadership capabilities, including an ability to appropriately prioritize and allocate resources, deploy sound judgment in complex situations, maintain a positive attitude in the face of adversity, and work effectively with others at multiple levels within the organization.
Strong written and oral communication skills, with clear and direct verbal reporting.
Proven track record of commitment to the success of others and full ownership and accountability of personal and functional performance.
